summary: All 42 automated checks pass. I read the CR-005 rules (sensing, reaction delay, speed targets, swerve completion, lock release, write-off, damage routing) and they match the specification. The hand-computed damage grid matches the build in all 60 cases. Several playtest and QA-report items are unverified because they need a person or figures the report does not contain (listed below). None of them is a defect.

criteria.evidence: Checks load_sim, params_match_spec (262 values), state_shape, sim_is_pure, deterministic_and_seeded, attract_then_confirm. I read sim.js: the mulberry-style rnd(s) uses state.rng, and sim.js has no Math.random, Date or DOM access. createSim honours the autostart and traffic options.

Checks lunge_distance_equal_8_directions (164.0 px in each direction), lunge_frame_rate_independent, lunge_eases_out (87% at half time), held_lunge_does_not_chain, recovery_is_tweened, walk_frame_rate_independent, run_speed_matches_spec. I read dummyStep: fresh press via prevLunge, cooldown, ease3 on the displacement difference, hall clamp, easeOutQuad recovery.

Checks level1_road_flows_left_to_right, level2_cross_no_collisions, level3_free_for_all, levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic, solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play, write_off_animation_then_card, level_progression, ending_decommissioned, ending_licensed, front_impact_pays_once, tail_contact_pays_its_small_share. I read spawnStep, drawEntry, axisMove, limits and levelEnd. Draw order is interval, entry, unit. Unit counts, allocations and level-end order are as specified.
level1_road_flows_left_to_right: 14 cars in 60 s, none stalled.
Check html_static. index.html has no http(s) references, loads sim.js with a script tag, uses a fixed 1/60 accumulator, and lists the Plex font names first with monospace fallbacks.
Playtest item. The code draws roads, level name and number, HUD, cards, attract screen, overlay toggle and restart. Math.random appears only in shake, particles and floating numbers.
Playtest item. Measured level lengths were 62 to 66 s on level 1, 78 to 83 s on level 2 and 89 to 97 s on level 3.
Checks damage_module_is_logical and damage_in_play_matches_module, plus my own hand check of the grid (damage_audit).

Checks dummy_cannot_walk_through_a_car and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play. I read pushOut, which uses face exits, nearestClear and a 4-pass loop. Barrier clearances were 9 px on level 1 and 3.02 px on level 2.
The shoulder-use batch figure is not in the report. The code supports it: limits() allows the shoulder band and swFeasible permits a swerve into it.

I read the stuck path. At the commit line, if neither side is feasible, stuck=true and lock stays 0. The brake factor 0.55/0.34 then applies. A locked car that becomes infeasible keeps its lock and brakes with B and no caution factor F. Check levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic shows no barrier crossings and no overlaps.
Checks level3_free_for_all and traffic_audit. latFree includes the oncoming-band test, and spawnStep makes spawns wait on the oncoming band.
Playtest items. drawShoulders and drawBarriers have the right geometry in code, including gaps at the junction, and draw nothing on level 3.
Check level2_cross_no_collisions (18 horizontal, 24 vertical cars). I read the arrows drawn in drawRoads and the left and top spawn edges in drawEntry.

Checks traffic_audit and vehicle_numbers_for_qa. I read stallStep: it never removes cars with a lower serial, resets when the lowest-serial car moves or sees the dummy, and leaves vehiclesSpawned unchanged. Level 3 breaker counts were 3 cars in 3 of 30 idle runs and 4 cars in 4 of 30 wandering runs. The longest hold was 10.4 s with a wandering dummy, which is possible because L.sees now covers 320 px. Reported only, as the specification directs.

Damage is pure and has exactly two functions. contactFace and assess take only their arguments. judge calls them once per contact and contains no damage arithmetic. No perMomentum, lungeBonus or faceNose names remain.

Checks damage_module_is_logical and hit_during_any_lunge_step_counts_as_a_lunge (161 hits, 0 on the final step, all scored as lunges), plus the hand-computed grid. I read outsidePoint and judge, which use the snapshot position for the zone (no tunnelling). judge sets lunging from d.lunging OR d.lungedThisStep.

I read Damage.assess: vs<=0 gives damage 0 and momentumFactor 0. judge still records lastImpact, sets hit and sets levelContact before returning when pay<=0. Health and score are untouched in that case.

Checks modules_exist_and_do_the_work and vehicle_numbers_for_qa. Rest to cruise measured 0.383 s for the sedan, matching expected. Lane deviation was 0 on all three levels. Per-step speed changes over the limit were all attributed to truncation (10 steps), none to other causes. In the code review, only Vehicles writes car.x/y/speed/lock/braking/sees/wary/aware/senseTime/lockT. judge writes only c.hit. Health changes only by res.damage.

The gate is only partly satisfied. Present: damage table, Lawrence cases, vehicle numbers, barrier clearances, stall-breaker counts, pillar sweep, settled speeds 82.8 and 69. Not in the report: write-off step counts at 1/60 and 1/120, the body-health figures (4 and 16 hits, service rate, severity 0.3125), the 30-seed count of cars committing before being aware, the AC-81 lock-release result and the AC-82 swerve-completion trace. I confirmed these by reading the code only.
Playtest item. The damage grid supports the intended ratios.

Check write_off_animation_then_card (1.10 s, frozen, confirm ignored, then card) and ending_licensed. I read step: in mode writeoff only time, fx timers and w.t advance, plus prevLunge and prevConfirm. At the end it sets writeOff=null, then writeOffEnd makes either a licensed ending or a card. The mode branches are else-if, so the card cannot be dismissed on the same step. A confirm is fresh only if prevConfirm was false, and index.html's confirm is a one-shot. Step counts at the two dt values were not reported.

Needs a person to judge the look. The code is as specified: shake 14*(1-u)^2, red blend over u/0.25, scale and alpha 1 - smooth(.35,.85,u), return when al<=0, 18 particles at 60 to 220 px/s with drag (reach about 116 px), cleared when the card appears.
index.html reads only S.writeOff.t / duration and keeps its own parts array. sim.js has no shake or particle code. The only animation state is mode and writeOff {t, duration, x, y}.
Playtest item.

PARAMS maxHealth and maxPay are both 1600, and the string 2300 does not appear in sim.js. Check params_match_spec passes. The first hit in the check front_impact_pays_once started from health 1600.0. Service repair is maxHealth/fullTime in dummyStep. Reach is 1-(1-wearFloor)*(1-h/max). Specific 4-hit, 16-hit and service-rate runs were not reported.
Playtest item.
PARAMS.perception equals the required six values (check params_match_spec). createSim clones the params into state.params.

Check perception_geometry: 64 points over 4 headings correct, learned 400 px range respected, and every row of the report table matches expected. I read senses(): the path zone is 0<a<max(detect,frontRange) with |b|<margin. The side wedge is |v|<=100 and v.heading>=|v|cos80, with an epsilon so the boundary counts as inside.

Check reaction_delay_then_unsure_then_committed shows aware after the reaction delay: 0.13 s (about 8 steps) at 60 Hz, 17 steps at 120 Hz, and 9 further steps after a break. These are within the +/-1 step tolerance. I read carsStep: senseTime accumulates while sees or wary and resets to 0 otherwise. aware = senseTime >= 0.15-1e-9. Give-way and barrier logic never read aware.

Checks side_sensor_makes_a_car_wary (sedan 82.8, van 72.0) and reaction_delay_then_unsure_then_committed (sedan 69.0, van 60.0). I read the target in carsStep: wary is cruise*0.6*F, unsure is min(0.5,B)*cruise*F, and F=1-0.4*min(1,|v|/runSpeed).

I read carsStep: the commit, the hatch flip and canSwerve all require c.aware. The lock is cleared only by the aActual<-(length/2+radius) test. The bus has swerve:false, so canSwerve is false and it never locks. The commit line uses the unit's own detect. The 30-seed random-input count of locks before awareness was not reported.

Check unnoticed_cars_ignore_the_dummy (cruise held at 138). I read the speed ladder: lock+stuck gives cruise*brake with no F; lock+complete gives cruise; lock+incomplete gives unsure*F; not aware gives cruise; aware and sees gives unsure*F; otherwise wary*F.
I read the braking line: speed fell, held, or (speed<cruise and target<=speed). Braking is false when the target is cruise and during the delay. The brake light is drawn from c.braking only.

Check outsmarting_pays_more_than_stand_and_lunge for the sedan: stand-and-lunge best 150 at 41 px/s, ambush from outside the sensors 500 at 138 px/s, first sensed at 317 px. The bait-then-lunge best was 300 as a frontCorner hit, not 500 from a nose hit. The scripted baited nose hit at full speed was not demonstrated, so the practical bait path is left to playtest (AC-85).

sideRadius, sideHalfAngleDeg, reactionDelay, the speed factors and frontRange are used only in senses, carsStep, the PARAMS literal and the renderer's read of frontRange and the side parameters. No new RNG draws. Damage is unchanged.

Playtest item. The drawCar code draws the wedge (lit on c.wary) and a rectangle of max(detect,frontRange) x 2*margin from the centre (lit on c.sees). It draws the commit line and chevron, a diamond aware cue with a 0.25 s ring, and brake lights from c.braking.
Playtest item. The sweep data support it: no stand-and-lunge hit above 150 for the sedan. Level 1 finishes in about 62 to 66 s with a standing dummy.

Check outsmarting: first sensed at a centre distance of 317 px, within 320 +/-5. The nose-gap sweep from 0 to 300 px has a maximum of 150, and every contact had awareBefore true. I read the code: the commit line is D.detect*cf and brake uses D.detect*brakeLead. The path range is max(detect,320), so learning cannot shorten it.

I read the code: conflict = senses(actual)==path OR senses(predicted)==path, and wary = !conflict && senses(actual)==side (the side result for the predicted point is ignored). The sweep shows a speed of 41 px/s at contact for the sedan. No per-step trace was in the report.

The only lock clear in the sim is the line `if(c.lock && aActual < -(c.length/2+radius))`, which uses the actual position. The 30-seed numeric check was not reported. I verified it by reading the code only.

I read the code: lockT is set at commit and at a flip, and complete is |lw0-lockT|<=2 measured at the start of the step. Until complete the target is the unsure target times F. The sweep shows lockBefore 1 at 41 px/s. No step-by-step trace was reported.
Check outsmarting sedan sweep: gaps 60 to 160 give 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 150, 90, 90, 0, 0 (maximum 150). The 0 to 20 px off-lane variant was not reported.

Check a_standing_dummy_is_steered_round: level 1 at y=284 and y=336 gave 19 cars each with 0 hits, which covers lane positions only. Level 2 gave 0 clips. Bus and sports front contacts are allowed by the check, as the specification expects for the bus and the late-committing sports car. The shoulder positions (y 230 and 390) were not reported.
Playtest item. The data show stand-and-lunge 150, ambush 500 and bait-then-lunge 300 for the sedan (652 for the van).

defects.problem: On level 3, swFeasible and limits() apply no hall bounds. A wide swerve (margin up to 190 px, or about 200 px for a closed unit) can take a car partly outside the hall laterally. This is not a CR-005 regression and is cosmetic.
The vans' stand-and-lunge best was 217 against the 175 bound. That bound is specified for the sedan only (AC-75, AC-79, AC-83). Noted for tuning.

cases.case: wagon (mf 1.2522) all zones, same as sports

damage_audit.comment: I computed every class and zone by hand as round(100*share*(1 or 5)*speed*mass/138) and all 60 values match (the first 20 cases are listed singly; the van, sports, wagon and hatch rows are grouped walking/lunging pairs). Shares fall nose > frontCorner > flank > rearCorner > tail. Lunging equals 5x walking up to rounding. Nothing exceeds the bus nose lunge (1174) and the cap is not reached. A stopped car pays 0, and a soft or slowed car pays proportionally less (vs>0 is required, and mf scales with vs). judge is the only place that changes health and score, and it does so only through Damage.assess's damage. lunge direction and speed are ignored.

vehicle_audit.paths: Cars keep to lane lines exactly when there is no sensing and nothing to yield to (lane deviation 0 on all three levels). Lateral motion comes only from commit swerves, the hatch flip and return to lane. Each is limited by limits() to the barrier band on levels 1 and 2, by latFree, and by axisMove truncation. Measured barrier clearance with a wandering dummy was 9 px on level 1 and 3.02 px on level 2. On level 3 there are no limits, so a wide swerve can leave the hall sideways. A locked car holds its offset until the dummy is behind its rear edge by more than 13 px.
vehicle_audit.stop_start: A car slows or stops for these reasons. (1) Give-way to a lower serial that is not behind it, with a target of 0 or the follower's speed. (2) Truncation against any car, which sets its speed to that car's speed. (3) Wary at 0.6 cruise, unsure at min(0.5,B) cruise, with F applied; this is not a stop. (4) Mid-swerve at the unsure speed. (5) Stuck, with brake 0.55 (0.34 for the bus), which is not a stop. Cars restart at accel 360 px/s^2 when the sweep test clears (rest to cruise 0.383 s for the sedan, matching expected). The dummy never stops a car, because the brake factors are above 0. Measured cruise-to-stop of about 3.9 s is longer than cruise/decel because the follower closes the final gap slowly (stopping without touching, gap about 7.9 px). The longest stop was 0 s on levels 1 and 2 and 13.7 s on level 3.
vehicle_audit.removal: Cars leave in two ways. (1) Exiting wholly past the travel-direction hall edge, the normal path. (2) The level 3 stall breaker, which deletes higher-serial cars adjacent to or in the sweep of the lowest-serial car once it has been held below 1 px/s for 6 s without seeing the dummy. This deletes cars to clear a jam. Measured: 5 cars removed inside the hall in 3 traffic runs, 3 cars in 3 of 30 idle-dummy runs and 4 cars in 4 of 30 wandering runs; none on levels 1 and 2. The longest hold of the lowest-serial car was 10.4 s with a wandering dummy. The specification says to report this and not fix it.
concerns: The level 3 stall breaker fired in 3 to 4 of 30 runs and deletes cars (reported, not fixed, per the specification).
The longest hold of the lowest-serial car was 10.4 s, above stallLimit+1. This is explained by the longer sensing zone resetting the breaker timer. It is outside the zone of the idle-dummy checks.
On level 3 a wide swerve is not bounded by the hall.

notes: Unverified, all needing a person: AC-24, AC-25, AC-36, AC-37, AC-55, AC-61, AC-63, AC-67, AC-77, AC-78 and AC-85. The pillar numbers hold on the sedan: stand-and-lunge 150, ambush 500.

Bait-then-lunge on the sedan reached only 300 as a frontCorner hit in the harness (the van reached 652). Playtest should confirm that a baited full nose hit on a sedan is achievable without extreme timing.

Not in the report, so confirmed only by reading the code: the write-off step counts at both dt values, the body-health figures, the 30-seed count of cars locking before awareness, the AC-81 numeric result, the AC-82 speed trace and the shoulder-position clip runs. Worth adding to the next QA run.
The mid-swerve slow-down lengthens pace slightly. Level 1 ended in 62 to 66 s with a standing dummy, a little under the designer's 70 to 90 s intent. Tuning only.
Van stand-and-lunge best was 217, above the 175 sedan bound. Not a criterion failure.
